items.title: Tom Albert Interview, 1962-05-07
items.q: I played when they didn't have no drums. Mm-hmm. Didn't have no drums when I played with Johnny Gould in there.

ctx.x: What's that? Johnny Gould, the first string band ever, you know, ragtime band ever heard. Then afterwards they come with the mother band, the Cucked Seeders and the string band with Manuel Perez and this fellow, Naum Manetta, one of them fellows that's in the old, that's before your time. So Naum Manetta, I bought his horn after he died. That was Manuel Manetta's uncle. Yeah, here it's been a long time. Oh yeah? Yeah, it's been a long time. I bought his horn.
Was that the first horn you ever had?

items.title: Tom Albert Interview, 1962-05-07
items.q: Yeah, oh yeah, Creole, yeah. He was real bright.

ctx.x: But he could, he was real bright, huh?
Yeah, oh yeah, Creole, yeah. He was real bright. Of course, what do you want to say?
Did you ever see any flagpole raisins with a band? Well, oh yeah, I seen a flagpole raisin.

items.title: Tom Albert and Milton "Mooney" Martin Interview, 1964-12-21
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] You remember Johnny Gould? No. That's an old band. No. That's an old band. [INTERVIEWEE] That's an old band.

ctx.x: Yeah, Johnny Lindsey, he used to play bass you know. Yeah, he played bass with his daddy. Yeah, with his daddy. What does his daddy play? His daddy used to play guitar. Guitar. Yeah, and his brother used to play violin. That was Herbert Russell. Herbert.

I knew Johnny, I knew Johnny but I never knew Herbert. But Herbert was still in Chicago a few years ago and I couldn't find him. Yeah. I tried to find him in 1958, six years ago. Yeah. And he was still there. He owned him. He might be dead now but he was there. No. I told you who saw him, you remember some singers, Mack and Mack? Mack and Mack, yeah. They were still up there and they said they saw him at a grocery store every once in a while but when they tried to find him they didn't see him. I was only there a…
Now you take, the old man he used to play with Peter Port.
